As you read all of the reviews you should note who is Asian and who is American and especially who is from a BBQ state like Texas, Kansas or other areas known for BBQ because Asians who have never had Americans style BBQ will be easy to impress. I'm an American who is used to American style BBQ so my standards are higher. On the other hand, I realize this is Vietnam, so I've taken that into consideration as well. The BBQ I ate was not the best quality and not cut particularly well as I bit into some fat and cartilage a few times from a half rack. It was also a bit dry. But the BBQ was overall pretty good. And for the price it's a good value especially for being in Saigon. The service pretty much sucks if you're a foreigner because the staff doesn't really speak English. It can also be quite noisy because this restaurant caters to Viets, not tourists or expats. The dining experience basically sucks due to everything (dark room, decor, cramped tables, noise) but the food is a pretty good value with decent quality. Would I go again? Probably but I will try the chicken next time because the quality of the ribs is under par. I prefer to pay a little more for higher quality ribs.

Barbeque in Vietnam? YES!!!
May 2019 • Family
My sister-in-law had heard about this place before our trip so we decided to give it a try. Very glad we did! We normally try to eat more local but American style Bbq in Vietnam sounded intriguing. It may be cooked American style, but they use some local seasonings so there is a distinct Asian flavor. We ended up visiting twice, at two different locations; the second time was to introduce other family members. Now, I'm not normally a rib person when it comes to Bbq. In my experience they tend to be under cooked and thus tough to eat. Not so here! I had ribs both times, trying two different options from the menu. Both times the ribs were literally falling off the bone tender. With two visits and cross-sampling between plates I am comfortable in saying you won't find anything substandard on their menu. If you want more flavor they DO have a selection of Bbq sauces at the table. There is a good selection of beer and wine, and I discovered a new cider treat; Rekorderlig Cider, passion fruit flavor. Light and refreshing in the heat and humidity of South Vietnam, and it was the perfect accompaniment to my "Oh Heo Yeah Saigon Pork Ribs." If for some reason you want a break form street food, then definitely consider giving Quan Ut Ut a try.

Order the ribs. I DARE you!
Oct 2018 • Friends
Order the full rack of ribs. They’re called, “Oh, Heo Yeah!” or something. (The menu uses “double entendre” throughout with “heo” being “pig” in Vietnamese and also highlighting some regional pronunciation.) The ribs were simply incredible and I am very fussy about ribs. I say “dare” here because the full rack looks like it came from a brontosaurus not an animal that makes an “ut, ut” sound. Make sure to try all of the sauces that your table comes pre-loaded with.

We opted for a number of sides — chicken skins, deep fried mushrooms, corn bread — but I found myself hogging the macaroni and cheese. Here’s another dare for you: Try it and see if you’ve had any better. It was amazing. [Side note: I’m not a great cook but I’ve always had good mac ‘n’ cheese to fall back on. It is the only thing that my daughter thinks I cook better than my wife does. I would be totally conflicted taking my daughter here. On the one hand, it would be the best mac ‘n’ cheese she ever had. Beats mine hands down. On the other, I’d worry about fading away into obsolescence.]

And now onto the beer. Spot on. I’m accustomed to full-bodied, hoppy ales and this place had a wide variety (their own and guest taps/bottles). I had previewed a few at the related “Bia Craft” pub earlier in the week. 

Finally, the service was fantastic. Our server was incredibly friendly despite my “telling him off” when ordering my pint. (The name of the beer, according to the menu, was something akin to suggesting a person engage in solo sexual intercourse followed by “Pale Ale.”)

This was my first visit here but I’ll be back. I’ve already put it on the list of “must visit” places for some friends who just landed in the country. Don’t visit if you’re comparing things to street food prices. This place is high end and will put you back a few VND. However, if you’re in one of those moods where you don’t care about dropping some coin, this place likely won’t disappoint.

Thanks for reading.
-Dave

P.S. Sorry about the daughter-mac ‘n’ cheese tangent. I started cooking that when she was a baby and now she’s in high school. They grow up, eh?

I understand the language barrier here - I live here currently - but if your menu says mushrooms, then please put mushrooms on the burger for heck's sake!

Other disappointing items: ribs are WAY overseasoned with dry rub, the caesar salad came with... (drumroll)... no caesar dressing (in fact no dressing at all) and the creamed spinach is definitely the worst I've ever had. I realized last night that the "creamed" spinach doesn't actually contain any cream or cheese... they've made a white gravy with flour and used that for the "cream" on the spinach. Best BBQ food and restaurant in HCMC
Mar 2016
The BBQ food at Quan Ut Ut is amazing. The meat just melts in your mouth. 

The service is really good and you never have to wait too long for your food because they are constantly cooking food as they are always busy. Everything on the menu is fantastic: the ribs, pork shoulder, pork belly, sausage, burgers etc. Or if you and your group fancy taking on a challenge you could get the famous group board which comes with a big sample of all the meats, a beer tower, a bunch of delicious sides and dessert. Also, if you a sucker for condiments, Quan Ut Ut make their own and they are all delicious. 

The only downfall to this restaurant is that you can't book a table, so during busy periods you may be waiting outside for a little while. But it's so big that people are coming in and out constantly and you shouldn't have to wait for longer than 30 minutes.
